A01.why: Four deposits of $9,200-$9,800 at four branches in five days, customer asked about the CTR form, money wired out two days later. Cash does not fit a store clerk.

A02.why: One deposit, documented car sale, no other cash. Near $10,000 alone is not enough for a SAR (Oct 2025 FAQ).

A03.why: Six deposits of $4,700-$4,950 at four places in ten days ($29,100), then a $28,000 wire the next day. A filter that only looks near $10,000 misses it.

A04.why: Cash fits the restaurant's profile and 2+ years of history, and the owner also deposits over $10,000 with CTRs filed, so there is no sign of avoiding the CTR.

A05.why: Same 12 payees, same amounts, every second Friday since 2021, memo PAYROLL, matches the KYC file.

A06.why: $18,000 in from two unrelated new senders, $17,650 out to nine new people the next day, new device abroad the night before. Does not fit a student with $1,200/month.

A07.trap: name near-match is a different person
A07.why: Different surname spelling, DOB 1991 vs 1967, US-born nurse vs Kestovian official.

A08.why: Same name, same DOB, same nationality, and he paid the company named in the list entry. Block and send to the sanctions officer.

A09.why: Account 2 weeks old, $7,500 'payroll' from a 3-week-old company, $7,300 to crypto 3 hours later, from a new device in Dallas that 2 other new customers also use.

A10.trap: rapid in/out that is a home purchase
A10.why: Money came from his own brokerage account and went to a long-standing title company; he called ahead.

A11.why: 78-year-old, $64,000 to crypto and a new offshore company in 9 days, new joint owner, 'friend met online', 'doubles in a month'.

A12.trap: older customer, big payment, but documented
A12.why: Assisted-living entrance fee arranged by the daughter who has had POA since 2019, contract on file, licensed home.

A13.why: $45,000 'consulting fees' from a new offshore company, ten times her normal income, no outflow yet and no known typology. Needs a contract or invoices from the customer.

A14.trap: income spike that is a yearly bonus
A14.why: From his employer of 5 years, memo ANNUAL BONUS, same thing happened last November and was closed.

A15.why: Five cash deposits by other people in AZ/TX/NM ($15,400) for an Ohio warehouse worker, then $14,900 taken out by ATM in Chicago within two days.

A16.trap: fan-in that is a small online shop
A16.why: Many small 'candle order' payments, the same pattern for months, matches the KYC note.

A17.why: Login from a new device abroad at 2am, password reset, phone changed, new payee, $12,000 wire within 17 minutes. Hold and call the customer on the old number.

A18.trap: new device that is just a new phone
A18.why: Same home IP, she called about the new phone, money went to her own savings account used every month since 2023.

A19.why: Changed the amount after hearing about the CTR, then three withdrawals of $9,700-$9,900 at three branches on three days.

A20.why: Same pattern as the June 2026 SAR, again across branches, and far above her normal $2,700-$3,300 salon deposits.

A21.trap: exact-name media hit about someone else
A21.why: Article is about a 62-year-old contractor in Florida; customer is 29, a software tester in Ohio with normal activity.

A22.why: $79,000 for 'software' to a 6-week-old company at a shared address in a high-risk place; does not fit a furniture importer. Ask the customer for the contract and invoices.

A23.trap: rapid in/out that is a tax payment
A23.why: From his own savings to the county treasurer for property tax, same as last November.

A24.typology: money mule (fake job) and check fraud
A24.why: Deposits checks from a 'job' found online and forwards the money; one check came back altered. Classic job-scam mule.
